question: A 10-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain. Four days ago, she visited a petting zoo with her family. Her temperature is 39.4°C (102.9°F). Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation of the right lower quadrant. Stool cultures at 42°C grow colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine. Which of the following best describes the most likely causal organism?

options.opa: Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose
options.opb: Gram-positive, anaerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that form spores
options.opc: Gram-negative, flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose
options.opd: Gram-positive, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that produce catalase
options.ope:
Gram-positive, aerobic, rod-shaped bacteria that form spores
"

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain" -> "Visited a petting zoo" -> "Temperature of 39.4°C" -> "Tenderness in right lower quadrant" -> "Stool cultures grow colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine" -> "Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose" -> 80% CHAIN: "Bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain" -> "Visited a petting zoo" -> "Temperature of 39.4°C" -> "Tenderness in right lower quadrant" -> "Stool cultures grow colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine" -> "Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose" -> "Possible Clostridium perfringens infection" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely causal organism in this case is Gram-negative, non-flagellated bacteria that do not ferment lactose, possibly Clostridium perfringens based on the stool culture results. The presence of colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine supports this conclusion.
analysis: The core medical principle guiding this case is the identification of the most likely causal organism based on the clinical presentation and stool culture results. The presence of bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and the growth of colonies that turn black after adding phenylenediamine suggest a Clostridium perfringens infection. Clostridium perfringens is a Gram-positive, anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium that forms spores. The enhanced information aligns with this conclusion.
